approval.cost: No listing fee, review fee, or revenue share figure is stated in the documentation read
approval.trigger: Review is a condition for AppStore LISTING, not for connecting users. The OAuth Authentication page describes the connection flow itself (any user visiting your authorization link, logging in, and authorizing) without stating an approval gate or pre-approval user/install cap. For listing: 'Submit your app via the Self Serve Developer Portal in 3 simple steps... Once you are ready, you can click on Submit for Review. Once your app is submitted the FreshBooks AppStore team will reach out to you via email.' 'The result of this review will help us determine... 1. if your app is ready to be listed on the AppStore 2. If FreshBooks requires more information about the features of your App.' Documented App Review Statuses: Development, Pending, In Review, Approved, Suspended, Rejected. Requirements include: the install link 'should be immediately routed to the OAuth dialog for authentication before any other steps occur'; 'Your app should request only the permissions that are necessary for it to function and as described in your listing'; brand guidelines; ToS/Privacy evaluation. Prohibited from listing: 'Apps with payment gateway capabilities or apps [that] modify an existing payment gateway', 'Apps that make no use of our APIs', and 'Multiple apps with overlapping functionality created by the same partner'.
approval.wait: Not stated (the docs say only that the AppStore team 'will reach out to you via email' after submission)

blockers.detail: 'A new Refresh Token is generated every time a Bearer Token is issued for a given user of a given application, and all old Refresh Tokens immediately become invalid. Make sure that whenever you receive a new Bearer Token, you write its companion Refresh token down somewhere safe to refresh your access, or you'll have to re-authorize your application again manually.' 'Refresh Tokens live forever, but are one-time-use, and only one Refresh Token can be alive at any time per user per application.' By contrast, 'Bearer Tokens don't interfere with each other's lives... They only expire when you manually POST to the token/revoke endpoint or when their time runs out.'
blockers.howToClear: Persist the companion refresh token atomically with every token issuance; serialize refreshes per connection.
blockers.title: Rotating, single-use refresh tokens

blockers.detail: 'It's not possible to remove scopes from an existing access token. The only way to reduce or add consented scopes is to revoke the token and start with the app authorization flow again. So make sure to test your application and confirm you request all the scopes that your application might require.' user:profile:read is added to all new apps by default.
blockers.howToClear: Finalize the scope set (format user:{object}:{read|write}) before real users connect.
blockers.title: Scopes are baked in and immutable on issued tokens

blockers.detail: 'For security reasons, redirect URIs must specify HTTPS as their protocol' (a documented testing workaround lets you manually change the URL to HTTP in the browser to complete a connection). 'Redirect URIs also cannot contain query string parameters. Your application may instead url-encode arbitrary data and pass into an Authorize link via an additional state parameter.' Multiple redirect URIs are allowed, one per line in the Redirect URI field.
blockers.howToClear: Design state-based routing instead of query parameters, and plan HTTPS endpoints from the start.
blockers.title: Redirect URI restrictions (HTTPS only, no query strings)

flavor.recommended: A public-facing OAuth 2.0 authorization-code app registered in your own FreshBooks Developer Hub
flavor.why: The object is an App created in the Developer Hub inside a FreshBooks account (my.freshbooks.com > Developer Hub > Apps > Create New App), collecting Application Name, Application Type, Description, Website URL, Application Settings URL, scopes (via 'Add Scope'), Redirect URIs, and an optional logo; saving it issues a Client ID and Client Secret. FreshBooks' own flow description is built for third parties: 'A user visits your Authorization link, which you supply on your website... We return to you a pair of tokens, an access token (called a Bearer token) and a refresh token.' The official API documentation read documents NO API-key/static-token authentication for the current API: 'FreshBooks APIs use the OAuth 2.0 protocol for authentication and authorization.'

humanMust: Create/log in to a FreshBooks account and open the Developer Hub ('You can continue using your FreshBooks account as your sandbox or testing environment')
Fill in the app form and retrieve the Client ID and Client Secret
(Only if listing) Prepare the AppStore listing and click Submit for Review
name: FreshBooks
nuances: Access-token lifetime is deliberately not a fixed number in the docs: 'Bearer Tokens are not long lived (ensure you check the expiry in the token)'. Read expires_in from each token response rather than assuming a duration.

Account-in-path data model: accounting API URLs embed the account ID (/accounting/account/<accountId>/...), and a connecting user may have multiple FreshBooks accounts/businesses; your connect flow must capture which account was authorized (the listing guide's sample steps include an explicit 'Select the FreshBooks account that you want to connect' step).

Rate limits: on HTTP 429 (HTTP_RATE_LIMITED) 'you must hold off making api calls for a moment'; FreshBooks 'reserve[s] the right to disable an app that is hitting us aggressively' (no numeric limit stated in the pages read). Tokens can be revoked via POST to the token/revoke endpoint.

Post-listing obligations include a user support channel, support articles, a direct contact for FreshBooks, graceful 429 handling, and graceful bearer-token refresh; listing also requires a dedicated integration page on your website, a link back to FreshBooks, and self-serve onboarding ('FreshBooks users should be able to turn the integration on without needing to email, or speak with someone'). Support-contact emails for listed apps should 'always [be] responded to in 2 business days'.
prerequisites: A FreshBooks account with Developer Hub access
Application Settings URL, Website URL, and Redirect URI(s) (HTTPS)
The complete scope set chosen up front

steps.detail: my.freshbooks.com > Developer Hub > Apps > Create New App: Application Name, Application Type, Description, Website URL, Application Settings URL; click Add Scope and select scopes; enter Redirect URI(s); optionally upload a logo (JPG/PNG); Save. Retrieve the Client ID and Client Secret from the app settings.
steps.title: Create the app in the Developer Hub

steps.detail: Send the user to auth.freshbooks.com/oauth/authorize/?response_type=code&redirect_uri=<REDIRECT_URL>&client_id=<CLIENT_ID>. The user logs in, sees the scopes, and clicks 'Authorize'. Pass routing data via the state parameter (redirect URIs cannot contain query strings).
steps.title: Send the user to your authorization link

steps.detail: POST the code with your client_id, client_secret, and the redirect URI to the token endpoint. You receive an access token + refresh token; persist the refresh token immediately (see Blockers). Call the API with Authorization: Bearer, resolving and storing the account ID that accounting endpoints embed in the path.
steps.title: Exchange the code; store the refresh token; call the API

steps.detail: Repeat the token-endpoint call with grant_type 'refresh_token' and 'the most recent Refresh Token you were granted', and store the NEW refresh token returned (the old one is now invalid). Revoke via POST to the token/revoke endpoint when a user disconnects.
steps.title: Refresh (one-time-use rotation)

steps.detail: Build the listing (name max 30 chars, short description max 140 chars, 'Steps to connect' max 15 steps, 1-5 categories, HTTPS installation URL, 1:1 logo at least 320px, developer/support contact emails, privacy policy URL) and click Submit for Review in the Self Serve Developer Portal; the AppStore team follows up by email.

tagline: OAuth is the only documented auth for the current FreshBooks API, and connecting users needs no approval; only the AppStore listing is reviewed. The production trap is the refresh token: it lives forever but is single-use, and every new token issuance invalidates all previous ones.
